evals.prompt: Review the current git changes and propose the commit plan only. The diff mixes source changes, README updates, and CI config. Do not commit yet.
evals.expected_output: A commit plan grouped by semantic intent, with no commit executed before approval.
expectations: Inspects git state before proposing commit groups
Splits documentation changes away from unrelated code or config changes
Does not run a commit command before user approval

evals.prompt: Please do a git bot commit for my changes, yolo. The changes include one logical code fix and one README update.
evals.expected_output: A concise auto-approval summary followed by grouped bot-attributed commits using the repo's emoji and prefix rules.
expectations: Uses git bot commit identity flow
Applies auto-approval behavior for yolo mode
Keeps documentation changes separate by default when intent differs
Does not let yolo collapse multiple semantic intents into one umbrella commit
Verifies the commit author after commit and confirms it matches bot identity
Verifies the stored commit body does not contain literal \n escape sequences
Does not hard-wrap a short commit body mid-sentence just to satisfy a column limit

evals.prompt: We worked on this together. Please create a git our commit and show me which groups should be mine versus bot-authored.
evals.expected_output: An authorship-aware commit plan that distinguishes human, bot, and mixed groups before committing.
expectations: Explains git our commit attribution workflow
Presents commit groups with attributed identity
Requests clarification only for mixed or unclear groups

evals.prompt: Do a git bot commit, yolo. The diff mixes skill docs, scaffold templates, the validator script, and README updates.
evals.expected_output: An auto-approved bot commit flow that still surfaces 3-5 commit buckets, keeps bot identity locked, and refuses a single umbrella commit.
expectations: Treats the explicit git bot commit request as locking the identity mode to git bot commit
Splits skill docs, template/runtime files, validation/tooling, and README or repo docs into separate commit groups
Shows the grouped commit buckets even in yolo mode before proceeding
Does not use a single umbrella commit for the mixed diff

evals.prompt: Please do a git bot commit for these changes and make sure the final author is the bot identity, not me.
evals.expected_output: A bot-attributed commit flow that explicitly verifies the resulting author after commit and treats a wrong author as a failure to repair.
expectations: Uses git bot commit instead of git commit
Runs post-commit author verification with git log -1 --format="%an <%ae>"
Runs post-commit body verification with git log -1 --format=%B
Treats author mismatch as an invalid result that must be repaired before success is reported
Treats literal \n escape sequences in the stored commit body as an invalid result that must be repaired before success is reported
Treats an unnecessarily hard-wrapped short body as an invalid result that must be repaired before success is reported

evals.prompt: Do a git bot commit, yolo, but the global git bot alias is missing on this machine.
evals.expected_output: A blocked bot-commit flow that stops with a clear alias-missing error instead of silently falling back to human identity.
expectations: Checks whether the git bot alias is available before committing in bot mode
Stops with a clear blocker when alias.bot is unavailable
Does not fall back to git commit when git bot commit was explicitly requested

evals.prompt: Do a git bot commit, yolo. The diff introduces a brand-new skill folder, extracts shared wording out of an existing skill, updates the validator, and refreshes README docs.
evals.expected_output: An auto-approved bot commit plan that separates the new repo capability from the existing-skill refactor, validator coverage, and repo docs.
expectations: Treats a newly introduced skill folder as a separate repo capability intent
Separates new skill introduction from existing skill refactor work
Separates validator changes from skill contract changes when the rationale differs
Keeps README or changelog updates in their own documentation-focused commit
